title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue That the People's Court of Second Instance Shall Review the Whole Case While Hearing the Appeal Filed by a Victim Against the Part of Civil Action Collateral to a Criminal Case and Shall Render a Final Judgment on the Part of Civil Action Collateral to Criminal Case

articles.content_en:
Reply of the Second Instance People's Court Concerning the Examination of the Entire Case and Rendering a Final Judgment on the Incidental Civil Action When the Victim Appeals Only the Civil Part of a Criminal Case
Fa (Yan) Fu [1988] No. 23
Higher People's Court of Shaanxi Province:
Your court's document Shaan Gao Fa Yan Zi [1988] No. 5, "Request for Instructions on How the Second Instance Court Shall Apply Legal Procedures When the Defendant in a Criminal Case with Incidental Civil Action Does Not Appeal but the Victim Appeals the Civil Part," has been received. Upon study, the reply is as follows:

In a criminal case with an incidental civil action, where the defendant does not appeal the criminal judgment and the People's Procuratorate does not file a protest, but only the victim, as the plaintiff in the incidental civil action, appeals the incidental civil part, the second instance People's Court shall review not only the incidental civil part but also the criminal part, in order to correctly determine the civil liability, and shall render a final judgment on the incidental civil part. The first instance criminal judgment shall take legal effect upon the expiration of the appeal period. If, during the second instance trial, it is found that the first instance criminal judgment is indeed erroneous, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the trial supervision procedure. If the criminal defendant who is to be delivered for enforcement of the sentence still needs to participate in the proceedings as the defendant in the incidental civil action in the second instance, for the convenience of the trial, the delivery for enforcement may be suspended until the second instance incidental civil part is concluded.

This reply.
May 11, 1988
